profile.name: CHE AMAH DILAND NGWA
profile.bio:
I am a Software Engineer and Chief Operating Officer at SAMITECH Corporation, focused on building high-impact, scalable solutions. Currently pursuing my Higher National Diploma in Software Engineering, I specialize in bridging technical execution with efficient operational strategy.

My expertise is rooted in the Python ecosystem, where I develop robust backend infrastructures and SaaS platforms. I am particularly interested in architectural challenges like data synchronization and system resilience. My design philosophy balances clean, logic-driven interfaces with high-performance server-side logic, turning conceptual ideas into market-ready products.

experience.title: Lead Software Engineer & COO | SAMITECH Corporation
experience.description: Leading distributed backend architecture, asynchronous event pipelines, and operational engineering roadmaps across SAMITECH's flagship SaaS platforms.
highlights: Technical Leadership (Lead Software Engineer) - Problem: Monolithic data pipelines and single-tenant database bottlenecks caused severe latency spikes and service outages during high-concurrency event bursts. Strategy: Engineered decoupled asynchronous event pipelines and multi-tenant database architectures using Python, FastAPI, and Docker. Impact: Reduced processing latency by over 60%, guaranteed strict multi-tenant data isolation, and unlocked seamless horizontal scaling under high system load.

Executive Operations & Product Strategy (COO) - Problem: Inconsistent engineering workflows and misaligned technical execution were lengthening feature delivery cycles and driving up cloud operational costs. Strategy: Established standardized DevOps CI/CD pipelines, redefined technical roadmaps to align with core business goals, and restructured developer sprint workflows. Impact: Reduced deployment cycle times, optimized cloud infrastructure expenditure, and accelerated time-to-market for flagship SaaS features.

projects.title: CodeForge
projects.tagline: Distributed Offline-First Code Execution & Sync Engine
projects.description: A resilient educational platform designed for low-connectivity environments, featuring a custom binary Delta synchronization engine and sandboxed code execution pipeline.
projects.challenge: Students and developers in emerging regions with erratic bandwidth faced high packet loss, multi-second feedback loops, and broken data synchronization states.
projects.solution: Architected a deterministic Priority-Queue delta sync protocol over WebSockets with Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) and local IndexedDB fallback, paired with a containerized Python/Wasm runtime.
projects.architecture: FastAPI microservices gateway with PostgreSQL write-ahead delta logs, Redis cache layer for active session state, and Dockerized worker pools for isolated code execution.
features: Priority-Queue delta synchronization protocol with automatic backoff
Sandboxed code execution runtime with memory & CPU quotas
Sub-30ms offline evaluation with bidirectional state merging
Scalable async worker architecture handling 5,000+ concurrent runs
Automated telemetry & edge-node health monitoring

endpoints.description: Batch sync offline state changes with CRDT vector clocks
Run untrusted Python script in isolated micro-VM

concurrencyTradeoffs.reason: Eliminates server-side lock contention entirely. Clients merge state offline deterministically without ever throwing merge conflicts or locking server threads.
benefits: 100% mathematical convergence across intermittent mobile drops
Drastic reduction in server CPU utilization during heavy editing spikes
tradeoffs: Slightly higher storage metadata overhead for vector clock history
Complex binary serialization logic required in both client and server runtimes

concurrencyTradeoffs.reason: Requires high-frequency synchronous round-trips to an authoritative coordinator. In emerging markets with 300ms+ jitter and 15% packet loss, user typing stalled constantly.
tradeoffs: Severely degraded UX on slow networks
Central coordinator becomes single point of failure under load

postMortem.incident: WebSocket connection storm following regional ISP reconnection
postMortem.impact: Gateway CPU surged to 92% as 4,000 mobile clients reconnected simultaneously within a 3-second window.
postMortem.rootCause: Clients reconnected immediately without randomized jitter, creating an synchronized thundering herd against the Redis vector store.
postMortem.resolution: Implemented exponential backoff with full jitter (Decorrelated Jitter algorithm) in the client SDK and added a token-bucket ingress rate limiter at the ASGI gateway.
postMortem.takeaway: Always assume clients in low-bandwidth regions will reconnect in synchronous waves after network outages.

Linear scalability with added worker containers
tradeoffs: Requires managing TTL expirations across distributed cache nodes

concurrencyTradeoffs.reason: Caused database lock waits and deadlock errors during large batch billing events at the start of each month.

postMortem.incident: Stripe webhook retry storm during worker deployment
postMortem.impact: Celery queue backed up by 120,000 tasks over 15 minutes.
postMortem.rootCause: Old workers shut down without graceful drain, causing in-flight unacknowledged tasks to be requeued multiple times.
postMortem.resolution: Configured Celery `worker_cancel_long_running_tasks_on_connection_loss` and set up graceful SIGTERM warm shutdowns in Docker entrypoint.
postMortem.takeaway: Always pair task acknowledgments (late acks) with idempotent handlers and graceful worker drainage.

concurrencyTradeoffs.approach: Redis Atomic Lua Scripting (Single-Threaded In-Memory Locks)
concurrencyTradeoffs.reason: Redis Lua executes completely atomically without yielding, guaranteeing that two concurrent requests for the last available item can NEVER both succeed.
benefits: Sub-2ms execution time per reservation attempt
Protects PostgreSQL from catastrophic row-locking contention
tradeoffs: Requires a separate reconciliation daemon to sync Redis stock levels back to PostgreSQL master

concurrencyTradeoffs.reason: Under 2,000+ concurrent requests on the same SKU, PostgreSQL transaction queues exploded, driving P99 checkout latency over 4,500ms and exhausting connection pools.
benefits: Single source of truth without caching
tradeoffs: Severe database deadlocks and timeouts during high-traffic drops

postMortem.incident: Expired cart reservations left orphaned stock in Redis during network timeout
postMortem.impact: 42 items appeared 'out of stock' for 30 minutes despite abandoned carts.
postMortem.rootCause: The TTL keyspace expiration event listener crashed silently, failing to return released reservation quantities back to the available pool.
postMortem.resolution: Replaced keyspace event dependence with deterministic Redis sorted sets (`ZSET`) scored by timestamp, paired with a cron-based release scrubber.
postMortem.takeaway: Never rely solely on Redis keyspace notifications for critical financial/inventory workflows, as pub/sub deliveries are fire-and-forget.
